verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["is hereby authorized"],"text":"(a) The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of \nthe Treasury and other officials of the United States Government as appro-\npriate, is hereby authorized to impose on a foreign person any of the sanctions \ndescribed in subsections (b) and (c) of this section, upon determining that \nthe person, on or after the date of this order: \n(i) is responsible for or complicit in, has directly or indirectly engaged \nin, or attempted to engage in, or financed the obstruction, disruption, \nor prevention of efforts to promote a Syria that is stable, unified, and \nat peace with itself and its neighbors, including: \n(A) the convening and conduct of a credible and inclusive Syrian- \nled constitutional process; \n(B) the preparation for and conduct of supervised elections, pursuant \nto the new constitution, that are free and fair and to the highest inter-\nnational standards of transparency and accountability; or \n(C) the development of a Syrian government that is representative and \nreflects the will of the Syrian people; \n(ii) is an adult family member of a person designated under subsection \n(a)(i) of this section; or \n(iii) is responsible for or complicit in, or has directly or indirectly engaged \nin, or attempted to engage in, the expropriation of property, including \nreal property, for personal gain or political purposes in Syria.’’"},{"char_end":11336,"char_start":10842,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":11336,"context_char_start":10842,"line":160,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary \nof the Treasury, shall examine whether the criteria set forth in section \n7431(a) of the Caesar Act have been met, and on the basis of that examination \nmay, pursuant to the Presidential Memorandum of March 31, 2020 (Delega-\ntion of Certain Functions and Authorities Under the National Defense Author-\nization Act for Fiscal Year 2020), suspend in whole or in part the imposition \nof sanctions otherwise required under the Caesar Act."},{"char_end":11675,"char_start":11337,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":11675,"context_char_start":11337,"line":166,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; Title 3 of the United States Code, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view of the continuing unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy of the United States upon which I based my declarations of national emergency in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979 and in Executive Order 12211, issued April 17, 1980, in order to implement agreements with the Government of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the Government of the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19, 1981, relating to the release of U.S. diplomats and nationals being held as hostages and to the resolution of claims of United States nationals against Iran, and to begin the process of normalization of relations between the United States and Iran and in which Iran and the United States instruct and require that the assets described in this Order shall be transferred as set forth below by the holders of such assets, it is hereby ordered that as of the effective date of this Order:"},{"char_end":3588,"char_start":3128,"text":"If the funds, securities, including Section 203 of the International Em ergency Eco­\nnomic Powers A ct (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States  \nCode, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the  \nNational Emergencies A ct (50 U.S.C. j.631), in view  of the continuing unusual  \nand extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy  \nof the United States upon which I based my declarations of national emergen­\ncy in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in Executive  \nOrder 12211, issued April 17,1980, in order to implement agreements with the  \nGovernment of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the Government of the  \nDemocratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19,1981, relating to  \nthe release of U.S. diplomats and nationals being held as hostages and to the  \nresolution of claims of United States nationals against Iran, and to begin the  \nprocess of normalization of relations between the United States and Iran and  \nin which Iran and the United States instruct and require that the assets  \ndescribed in this Order shall be transferred as set forth below by the holders  \nof such assets, it is hereby ordered that as of the effective date of this Order:\n1-101."},{"char_end":4283,"char_start":3793,"text":"If the funds, securities, and deposits described in section 1-101 are not  \npromptly transferred to the control of the Government of Iran, such funds,  \nsecurities, and deposits shall be returned to the banking institutions holding  \nthem on the effective date of this Order and the set-offs described in section  \n1-102 shall be in force as if this Order had not been issued and the status of all  \nsuch funds, securities, deposits and set-offs shall be s t a t u s  q u o  a n te .\n1-104."},{"char_end":6921,"char_start":6879,"text":"This Order shall be effective immediately."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12170>EO:12278@f3de9e28f41b68ec","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:12170>EO:12279**; Scf27532746fa65420bf68d28; {"actor_id":"EO:12279","char_end":2109,"char_start":630,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"on_signing","effective_date":"1981-01-19","effective_wording":[{"char_end":2109,"char_start":630,"text":"Executive Order 12279 of January 19, 1981\nDirection To Transfer Iranian Government A ssets Held by  \nDomestic Banks\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  \nthe United States, including Section 203 of the International Em ergency Eco­\nnomic Powers A ct (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 22 of the United States  \nCode, Section 1732 of 3 Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of  \nthe National Emergencies A ct (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view of the continuing  \nunusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and  \neconomy of the United States upon which I based my declarations of national  \nemergency in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in  \nExecutive Order 12211, issued April 17, 1980, in order to implement agree­\nments with the Government of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the  \nGovernment of the Dem ocratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January  \n19, 1981, relating to the release of U.S. diplomats and nationals being held as  \nhostages and to the resolution of claims of United States nationals against  \nIran, and to begin the process of normalization of relations betw een the  \nUnited States and Iran and in which Iran and the United States instruct and  \nrequire that the assets described in this Order shall be transferred as set forth  \nbelow by the holders of such assets, it is hereby ordered that as of the  \neffective date of this Order:\n1-101."},{"char_end":2932,"char_start":2110,"text":"Any branch or office of a banking institution subject to the jurisdiction  \nof the United States, which branch or office is located within the United States  \nand is, on the effective date, either (a) in possession of funds or securities  \nlegally or beneficially owned by the Government of Iran or its agencies,  \ninstrumentalities, or controlled entities, or (b) carrying on its books deposits  \nstanding to the credit of or beneficially owned by such Government, agencies,  \ninstrumentalities, or controlled entities is licensed, authorized, directed and  \ncompelled to transfer such funds, securities, and deposits, including interest  \nfrom November 14, 1979, at commercially reasonable rates, to the Federal  \nReserve Bank of New York, to be held or transferred as directed by the  \nSecretary of the Treasury.\n1-102."},{"char_end":5520,"char_start":5478,"text":"This Order shall be effective immediately."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12170>EO:12279","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Express signing-date wording; supplied signing date still needs source confirmation.","provision_label":"","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1981-01-19","target_id":"EO:12170","verb":"transfer"}

Order 12280 of January 19, 1981\nDirection To Transfer Iranian Government Financial A ssets  \nHeld by Non-Banking Institutions\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  \nthe United States, including Section 203 of the International Emergency Eco­\nnomic Powers A ct (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States  \nCode, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the  \nNational Emergencies A ct (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view  of the continuing unusual  \nand extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy  \nof the United States upon which I based my declarations of national emergen­\ncy in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in Executive  \nOrder 12211, issued April 17,1980, in order to implement agreements with the  \nGovernment of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the Government of the  \nDem ocratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated \nprocess of normalization of relations betw een the United States and Iran and  \nin which Iran and the United States instruct and require that the assets  \ndescribed in this Order shall be not an official edition); APP node 249531; common-crawl capture 2024-10-04T03:26:44Z","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"5abfe7c76eea271aa48b0f7f8e7fc7159a475583ca4b77013a0c3e2bb683b30b","signing_date":"1980-04-17","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-job-app-executive-orders-12211-5abfe7c76e.txt","text_sha256":"4766c050f3ddac533f9089d643608bdb21490dcd35fb8c04fcff8f65a378b976","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-12211-sanctions-against-iran"},"verb":"revoke"},{"actor_id":"EO:12276","char_end":4198,"char_start":56,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:12170#3","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of the United States, including Section 203 of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view of the continuing unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy of the United States upon which I based my declarations of national emergency in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in Executive Order 12211, issued April 17, 1980, in order to implement agreements with the Government of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the Government of the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19, 1981, relating to the release of U.S. diplomats and nationals being held as hostages and to the resolution of claims of United States nationals against Iran, and to begin the process of normalization of relations between the United States and Iran, it is hereby ordered that as of the effective date of this Order:\n\n1-101. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to enter into, and to license, authorize, direct, and compel any appropriate official and/or the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, as fiscal agent of the United States, to enter into escrow or related agreements with a foreign central bank and with the Central Bank of Algeria under which certain money and other assets, as and when directed by the Secretary of the Treasury, shall be credited by the foreign central bank to an escrow account on its books in the name of the Central Bank of Algeria, for transfer to the Government of Iran if and when the Central Bank of Algeria receives from the Government of Algeria a certification that the 52 U.S. diplomats and nationals being held hostage in Iran have safely departed from Iran. Such agreements shall include other parties and terms as determined by the Secretary of the Treasury to be appropriate to carry out the purposes of this Order.\n\n1-102. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to license, authorize, direct, and compel the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, as fiscal agent of the United States, to receive certain money and other assets in which Iran or its agencies, instrumentalities, or controlled entities have an interest and to hold or transfer such money and other assets, and any interest earned thereon, in such a manner as he deems necessary to fulfill the rights and obligations of the United States under the Declaration of the Government of the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19, 1981, and the escrow and related agreements described in paragraph 1-101 of this Order. Such money and other assets may be held in interest-bearing form and where possible shall be invested with or through the entity holding the money or asset on the effective date of this Order.\n\n1-103. Compliance with this Executive Order, any other Executive Order licensing, authorizing, directing or compelling the transfer of the assets referred to in paragraphs 1-101 and 1-102 of this Order, or any regulations, instructions, or directions issued thereunder shall to the extent thereof be a full acquittance and discharge for all purposes of the obligation of the person making the same. No person shall be held liable in any court for or with respect to anything done or omitted in good faith in connection with the administration of, or pursuant to and in reliance on, such orders, regulations, instructions, or directions.\n\n1-104. The Attorney General shall seek to intervene in any litigation within the United States which arises out of this Order and shall, among other things, defend the legality of, and all actions taken pursuant to, each of its provisions.\n\n1-105. The Secretary of the Treasury is delegated and authorized to exercise all functions vested in the President by the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) to carry out the purposes of this Order.\n\n1-106. This Order shall be effective immediately.\n\nJIMMY CARTER","sections_touched":["Section 203","Section 301","Section 1732","Section 301","paragraph 1","paragraphs 1"],"signing_date":"1981-01-19","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"archival_id":"app:node/250925","filing_date":null,"grade":"mirror_transcription","instrument_id":"EO:12276","location_confidence":"medium","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"Executive Order 12276—United States-Iran Agreement on Release of the American Hostages; wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of the United States, including Section 203 of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1702), Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code, Section 1732 of Title 22 of the United States Code, and Section 301 of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1631), in view of the continuing unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy and economy of the United States upon which I based my declarations of national emergency in Executive Order 12170, issued November 14, 1979, and in Executive Order 12211, issued April 17, 1980, in order to implement agreements with the Government of Iran, as reflected in Declarations of the Government of the Democratic and Popular Republic of Algeria dated January 19, 1981, relating to the release of U.S. diplomats and nationals being held as hostages and to the resolution of claims of United States nationals against Iran, and to begin the process of normalization of relations between the United States and Iran, it is hereby ordered that as of the effective date of this Order:\n\n1-101. For the purpose of protecting the rights of litigants in courts within the United States, all property and assets located in the United States within the control of the estate of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, the former Shah of Iran, or any close relative of the former Shah served as a defendant in litigation in such courts brought by Iran seeking the return of property alleged to belong to Iran, is hereby blocked as to each such estate or person until all such litigation against such estate or person is finally terminated.\n\n1-102. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized and directed (a) to promulgate regulations requiring all persons who are subject to the jurisdiction of the United States and who, as of November 3, 1979, or as of this date, have actual or constructive possession of property of the kind described in Section 1-101, or knowledge of such possession by others, to report such possession or knowledge thereof, to the Secretary of the Treasury in accordance with such regulations and (b) to make available to the Government of Iran or its designated agents all identifying information derived from such reports to the fullest extent permitted by law. Such reports shall be required as to all individuals described in 1-101 and shall be required to be filed within 30 days after publication of a notice in the FEDERAL REGISTER.\n\n1—103. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized and directed (a) to require all agencies within the Executive Branch of the United States Government to deliver to the Secretary all official financial books and records which serve to identify any property of the kind described in Section 1-101 of this Order, and (b) to make available to the Government of Iran or its designated agents all identifying information derived from such books and records to the fullest extent permitted by law.\n\n1-104. The Attorney General of the United States having advised the President of his opinion that no claim on behalf of the Government of Iran for recovery of property of the kind described in Section 1-101 of this Order should be considered legally barred either by sovereign immunity principles or by the act of state doctrine, the Attorney General is authorized and directed to prepare, and upon the request of counsel representing the Government of Iran to present to the appropriate court or courts within the United States, suggestions of interest reflecting that such is the position of the United States, and that it is also the position of the United States that Iranian decrees and judgments relating to the assets of the former Shah and the persons described in Section 1-101 should be enforced by such courts in accordance with United States law.\n\n1-105. The Secretary of the Treasury is delegated and authorized to exercise all functions vested in the President by the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) to carry out the purposes of this Order.\n\n1-106. This Order shall be effective immediately.\n\nJIMMY CARTER","sections_touched":["Section 203","Section 301","Section 1732","Section 301","Section 1","Section 1","Section 1","Section Re-examination of Members and  \nFormer Members of the Uniformed  \nServices”, as follows, such amendments  \nto be effective October 15, 1952:\nSection 3 of such order is amended to  \nread as follows; “All duties, powers, and  \nfunctions incident to the hospitalization,  \nexcept as provided in section 5 of this  \norder, and re-examination of members  \nof the uniformed services placed \nread as follows: “All duties, powers, and  \nfunctions incident to the hospitalization  \nof members or former members of the  \nuniformed services placed on the tempo­\nrary disability retired list or permanently  \nretired for physical disability or receiving  \ndisability retirement pay who require  \nhospitalization for chronic diseases shall  \nbe vested in the Administrator of Vet-\nerans’  Affairs: Provided,  that all duties,  \npowers, and functions incident to the  \nhospitalization of such members or  \nformer members who are or have been ad­\nmitted to hospitals under the jurisdiction  \nof the uniformed services before October  \n15, 1952, may be exercised by the Secre­\ntary concerned until April 15,1953: Pro­\nvided further,  that all the duties, powers,  \nand functions incident to hospitalization  \nfor such members or former members  \nwho have completed twenty or more  \nyears of active duty, as defined in section  \n412 of the Career Compensation Act of  \n1949, who require hospitalization for  \nchronic diseases other than blindness,  \nneuropsychiatrie or psychiatric disorders  \nand tuberculosis, who are acceptable  \nmedically to the Commanding Officer of a  \nservice hospital, and who elect not to  \nreceive hospitalization in Veterans Ad­\nministration facilities shall be vested in  \nthe Secretary concerned: And provided  \nfurther,  that for the purpose of this  \norder, the term ‘ chronic diseases’  shall be \nconstrued to include chronic arthritis,  \nmalignancy, psychiatric or neuropsychi­\natrie disorder, neurological disabilities,  \npoliomyelitis with disability residuals  \nand degenerative diseases of the nervous  \nsystem, severe injuries to the nervous  \nsystem including quadriplegics, hémi­\nplégies, and  \nAdministrator of Veterans’  Affairs, and  \nthe Federal Security Administrator and  \nso described in appropriate regulations  \nof the respective departments and agen­\ncies Re-examination of Members and  \nFormer Members of the Uniformed  \nServices”, as follows, such amendments  \nto be effective October 15, 1952:\nSection 3 of such order is amended to  \nread as follows; “All duties, powers, and  \nfunctions incident to the hospitalization,  \nexcept as provided in section 5 of this  \norder, and re-examination of members  \nof the uniformed services placed  \n1949, who require hospitalization for  \nchronic diseases other than blindness,  \nneuropsychiatrie or psychiatric disorders  \nand tuberculosis, who are acceptable  \nmedically to the Commanding Officer of a  \nservice hospital, and who elect not to  \nreceive hospitalization in Veterans Ad­\nministration facilities shall be vested in  \nthe Secretary concerned: And provided  \nfurther,  that for the purpose of this  \norder, the term ‘ chronic diseases’  shall be \nconstrued to include chronic arthritis,  \nmalignancy, psychiatric or neuropsychi­\natrie disorder, neurological - **ACT:EO:10122>EO:12086**; S9370ff85220bff25062c692a; {"actor_id":"EO:12086","char_end":1426,"char_start":1113,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":13044,"char_start":12859,"text":"The transfers or reassignments provided by Section 1-1 o f this \nOrder shall take effect at such time or times as the Director o f the Office o f \nManagement and Budget shall determine."},{"char_end":13147,"char_start":13045,"text":"The Director shall ensure that all \nsuch transfers or reassignments take effect within 60 days.\n1-302."},{"char_end":13512,"char_start":13148,"text":"The conforming amendments provided by Section 1-2 o f this \nOrder shall take effect on October 8, 1978; except that, with respect to those \nagencies identified in Section 1-101 o f this Order, the conforming amend­\nments shall be effective on the effective date o f the transfer or reassignment o f \nfunctions as specified pursuant to Section 1-301 o f this Order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10122>EO:12086","names_target":false,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. - **ACT:EO:10122>EO:12630**; S6497640c4c2668b1a76367c5; {"actor_id":"EO:12630","char_end":134796,"char_start":133953,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"relative","effective_date":"1988-06-13","effective_wording":[{"char_end":3772,"char_start":3694,"text":"Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries\nEffective Date of 1996 Amendment\nPub."},{"char_end":4363,"char_start":3907,"text":"L. 104–121, amending this section and sections 603 to 605, 609, 611, and 612 of this title and enacting provisions set out as a note under section 609 of this title] shall become effective on the expiration of 90 days after the date of enactment of this subtitle [Mar. 29, 1996], except that such amendments shall not apply to interpretative rules for which a notice of proposed rulemaking was published prior to the date of enactment.”\nEffective Date\nPub."},{"char_end":4775,"char_start":4364,"text":"L. 96–354, § 4, Sept. 19, 1980, 94 Stat. 1170, provided that: “The provisions of this Act [enacting this chapter] shall take effect January 1, 1981, except that the requirements of sections 603 and 604 of title 5, United States Code (as added by section 3 of this Act) shall apply only to rules for which a notice of proposed rulemaking is issued on or after January 1, 1981.”\nShort Title of 1996 Amendment\nPub."},{"char_end":14606,"char_start":13621,"text":"PURPOSES.\n“The purposes of this title are—\n“(1)\n to implement certain recommendations of the 1995 White House Conference on Small Business regarding the development and enforcement of Federal regulations;\n“(2)\n to provide for judicial review of chapter 6 of title 5, United States Code;\n“(3)\n to encourage the effective participation of small businesses in the Federal regulatory process;\n“(4)\n to simplify the language of Federal regulations affecting small businesses;\n“(5)\n to develop more accessible sources of information on regulatory and reporting requirements for small businesses;\n“(6)\n to create a more cooperative regulatory environment among agencies and small businesses that is less punitive and more solution-oriented; and\n“(7)\n to make Federal regulators more accountable for their enforcement actions by providing small entities with a meaningful opportunity for redress of excessive enforcement activities.\n“subtitle a—\nregulatory compliance simplification\n“SEC. 211."},{"char_end":17343,"char_start":14989,"text":"COMPLIANCE GUIDES.\n“(a)\n Compliance Guide.—\n“(1)\n In general.—\nFor each rule or group of related rules for which an agency is required to prepare a final regulatory flexibility analysis under section 605(b) [probably should be “section 604”] of title 5, United States Code, the agency shall publish 1 or more guides to assist small entities in complying with the rule and shall entitle such publications ‘small entity compliance guides’.\n“(2)\n Publication of guides.—\nThe publication of each guide under this subsection shall include—\n“(A)\n the posting of the guide in an easily identified location on the website of the agency; and\n“(B)\n distribution of the guide to known industry contacts, such as small entities, associations, or industry leaders affected by the rule.\n“(3)\n Publication date.—\nAn agency shall publish each guide (including the posting and distribution of the guide as described under paragraph (2))—\n“(A)\n on the same date as the date of publication of the final rule (or as soon as possible after that date); and\n“(B)\n not later than the date on which the requirements of that rule become effective.\n“(4)\n Compliance actions.—\n“(A)\n In general.—\nEach guide shall explain the actions a small entity is required to take to comply with a rule.\n“(B)\n Explanation.—\nThe explanation under subparagraph (A)—\n“(i)\n shall include a description of actions needed to meet the requirements of a rule, to enable a small entity to know when such requirements are met; and\n“(ii)\n if determined appropriate by the agency, may include a description of possible procedures, such as conducting tests, that may assist a small entity in meeting such requirements, except that, compliance with any procedures described pursuant to this section does not establish compliance with the rule, or establish a presumption or inference of such compliance.\n“(C)\n Procedures.—\nProcedures described under subparagraph (B)(ii)—\n“(i)\n shall be suggestions to assist small entities; and\n“(ii)\n shall not be additional requirements, or diminish requirements, relating to the rule.\n“(5)\n Agency preparation of guides.—\nThe agency shall, in its sole discretion, taking into account the subject matter of the rule and the language of relevant statutes, ensure that the guide is written using sufficiently plain language likely to be understood by affected small entities."},{"char_end":18827,"char_start":17538,"text":"An agency may prepare guides and apply this section with respect to a rule or a group of related rules.\n“(6)\n Reporting.—\nNot later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007 [May 25, 2007], and annually thereafter, the head of each agency shall submit a report to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship of the Senate, the Committee on Small Business of the House of Representatives, and any other committee of relevant jurisdiction describing the status of the agency’s compliance with paragraphs (1) through (5).\n“(b)\n Comprehensive Source of Information.—\nAgencies shall cooperate to make available to small entities through comprehensive sources of information, the small entity compliance guides and all other available information on statutory and regulatory requirements affecting small entities.\n“(c)\n Limitation on Judicial Review.—\nAn agency’s small entity compliance guide shall not be subject to judicial review, except that in any civil or administrative action against a small entity for a violation occurring after the effective date of this section, the content of the small entity compliance guide may be considered as evidence of the reasonableness or appropriateness of any proposed fines, penalties or damages.\n“SEC. 213."},{"char_end":21585,"char_start":21350,"text":"EFFECTIVE DATE.\n“This subtitle and the amendments made by this subtitle shall take effect on the expiration of 90 days after the date of enactment of this subtitle [Mar. 29, 1996].\n“subtitle b—\nregulatory enforcement reforms\n“SEC. 221."},{"char_end":24315,"char_start":24088,"text":"EFFECTIVE DATE.\n“This subtitle and the amendments made by this subtitle shall take effect on the expiration of 90 days after the date of enactment of this subtitle [Mar. 29, 1996].”\nEffects of Deregulation On Rural America\nPub."},{"char_end":46104,"char_start":45885,"text":"Each executive department and agency shall undertake to eliminate not less than 50 percent of its civilian internal management regulations that are not required by law within 3 years of the effective date of this order."},{"char_end":47965,"char_start":47332,"text":"No. 14215, § 3(a), Feb. 18, 2025, 90 F.R. 10448, provided:\nThe American people deserve a regulatory system that works for them, not against them: a regulatory system that protects and improves their health, safety, environment, and well-being and improves the performance of the economy without imposing unacceptable or unreasonable costs on society; regulatory policies that recognize that the private sector and private markets are the best engine for economic growth; regulatory approaches that respect the role of State, local, and tribal governments; and regulations that are effective, consistent, sensible, and understandable."},{"char_end":51474,"char_start":51256,"text":"(5) When an agency determines that a regulation is the best available method of achieving the regulatory objective, it shall design its regulations in the most cost-effective manner to achieve the regulatory objective."},{"char_end":60329,"char_start":59828,"text":"In order to have an effective regulatory program, to provide for coordination of regulations, to maximize consultation and the resolution of potential conflicts at an early stage, to involve the public and its State, local, and tribal officials in regulatory planning, and to ensure that new or revised regulations promote the President’s priorities and the principles set forth in this Executive order, these procedures shall be followed, to the extent permitted by law: (a) Agencies’ Policy Meeting."},{"char_end":67555,"char_start":66318,"text":"In order to reduce the regulatory burden on the American people, their families, their communities, their State, local, and tribal governments, and their industries; to determine whether regulations promulgated by the executive branch of the Federal Government have become unjustified or unnecessary as a result of changed circumstances; to confirm that regulations are both compatible with each other and not duplicative or inappropriately burdensome in the aggregate; to ensure that all regulations are consistent with the President’s priorities and the principles set forth in this Executive order, within applicable law; and to otherwise improve the effectiveness of existing regulations: (a) Within 90 days of the date of this Executive order, each agency shall submit to OIRA a program, consistent with its resources and regulatory priorities, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified or eliminated so as to make the agency’s regulatory program more effective in achieving the regulatory objectives, less burdensome, or in greater alignment with the President’s priorities and the principles set forth in this Executive order."},{"char_end":70127,"char_start":69890,"text":"The Regulatory Policy Officer shall be involved at each stage of the regulatory process to foster the development of effective, innovative, and least burdensome regulations and to further the principles set forth in this Executive order."},{"char_end":73926,"char_start":72240,"text":"(C) For those matters identified as, or determined by the Administrator of OIRA to be, a significant regulatory action within the scope of section 3(f)(1), the agency shall also provide to OIRA the following additional information developed as part of the agency’s decision-making process (unless prohibited by law):\n(i) An assessment, including the underlying analysis, of benefits anticipated from the regulatory action (such as, but not limited to, the promotion of the efficient functioning of the economy and private markets, the enhancement of health and safety, the protection of the natural environment, and the elimination or reduction of discrimination or bias) together with, to the extent feasible, a quantification of those benefits;\n(ii) An assessment, including the underlying analysis, of costs anticipated from the regulatory action (such as, but not limited to, the direct cost both to the government in administering the regulation and to businesses and others in complying with the regulation, and any adverse effects on the efficient functioning of the economy, private markets (including productivity, employment, and competitiveness), health, safety, and the natural environment), together with, to the extent feasible, a quantification of those costs; and\n(iii) An assessment, including the underlying analysis, of costs and benefits of potentially effective and reasonably feasible alternatives to the planned regulation, identified by the agencies or the public (including improving the current regulation and reasonably viable nonregulatory actions), and an explanation why the planned regulatory action is preferable to the identified potential alternatives."},{"char_end":91123,"char_start":88949,"text":"(c) The principal functions of the Interagency Working Group shall include:\n(i) coordinating the interagency review of any significant issues concerning the implementation of this order and analysis and recommendations in connection with pursuing the ratification of human rights treaties, as such questions may from time to time arise;\n(ii) coordinating the preparation of reports that are to be submitted by the United States in fulfillment of treaty obligations;\n(iii) coordinating the responses of the United States Government to complaints against it concerning alleged human rights violations submitted to the United Nations, the Organization of American States, and other international organizations;\n(iv) developing effective mechanisms to ensure that legislation proposed by the Administration is reviewed for conformity with international human rights obligations and that these obligations are taken into account in reviewing legislation under consideration by the Congress as well;\n(v) developing recommended proposals and mechanisms for improving the monitoring of the actions by the various States, Commonwealths, and territories of the United States and, where appropriate, of Native Americans and Federally recognized Indian tribes, including the review of State, Commonwealth, and territorial laws for their conformity with relevant treaties, the provision of relevant information for reports and other monitoring purposes, and the promotion of effective remedial mechanisms;\n(vi) developing plans for public outreach and education concerning the provisions of the ICCPR, CAT, CERD, and other relevant treaties, and human rights-related provisions of domestic law;\n(vii) coordinating and directing an annual review of United States reservations, declarations, and understandings to human rights treaties, and matters as to which there have been nontrivial complaints or allegations of inconsistency with or breach of international human rights obligations, in order to determine whether there should be consideration of any modification of relevant reservations, declarations, and understandings to human rights treaties, or United States practices or laws."},{"char_end":96369,"char_start":96248,"text":"One-size-fits-all approaches to public policy problems can inhibit the creation of effective solutions to those problems."},{"char_end":98080,"char_start":97894,"text":"Executive Order 12372 of July 14, 1982 (“Intergovernmental Review of Federal Programs”) [31 U.S.C. 6506 note] remains in effect for the programs and activities to which it is applicable."},{"char_end":102562,"char_start":102247,"text":"Within 90 days after the effective date of this order, the head of each agency shall designate an official with principal responsibility for the agency’s implementation of this order and that designated official shall submit to the Office of Management and Budget a description of the agency’s consultation process."},{"char_end":107087,"char_start":106794,"text":"(c) Within 180 days after the effective date of this order, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Assistant to the President for Intergovernmental Affairs shall confer with State and local officials to ensure that this order is being properly and effectively implemented."},{"char_end":107880,"char_start":107809,"text":"(c) This order shall be effective 90 days after the date of this order."},{"char_end":125349,"char_start":124836,"text":"In formulating and implementing policies that have implications for faith-based and other neighborhood organizations, agencies that administer social service programs or that support (including through prime awards or sub-awards) social service programs with Federal financial assistance shall, to the extent permitted by law, be guided by the following fundamental principles:\n(a) Federal financial assistance for social service programs should be distributed in the most effective and efficient manner possible."},{"char_end":168478,"char_start":167956,"text":"(b) Within 120 days of the date of this order, each agency shall develop and submit to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs a preliminary plan, consistent with law and its resources and regulatory priorities, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed so as to make the agency’s regulatory program more effective or less burdensome in achieving the regulatory objectives."},{"char_end":171822,"char_start":171300,"text":"(b) Within 120 days of the date of this order, each independent regulatory agency should develop and release to the public a plan, consistent with law and reflecting its resources and regulatory priorities and processes, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed so as to make the agency’s regulatory program more effective or less burdensome in achieving the regulatory objectives."},{"char_end":175796,"char_start":175531,"text":"They must provide for transparency and accountability by utilizing cost-effective information technology to collect and disseminate information about individual projects and agency performance, so that the priorities and concerns of all our citizens are considered."},{"char_end":176245,"char_start":176009,"text":"They must recognize the critical role project sponsors play in assuring the timely and cost-effective review of projects by providing complete information and analysis and by supporting, as appropriate, the costs associated with review."},{"char_end":177165,"char_start":177056,"text":"Permitting and review process improvements that have proven effective must be expanded and institutionalized."},{"char_end":177661,"char_start":177166,"text":"(b) In advancing this policy, this order expands upon efforts undertaken pursuant to Executive Order 13580 of July 12, 2011 (Interagency Working Group on Coordination of Domestic Energy Development and Permitting in Alaska), Executive Order 13563 of January 18, 2011 (Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review), and my memorandum of August 31, 2011 (Speeding Infrastructure Development Through More Efficient and Effective Permitting and Environmental Review), as well as other ongoing efforts."},{"char_end":182488,"char_start":181370,"text":"The Federal Plan shall include, but not be limited to, the following actions to implement the policies outlined in section 1 of this order, and shall reflect the agreement of any Member Agency with respect to requirements in the Federal Plan affecting such agency:\n(i) institutionalizing best practices for: enhancing Federal, State, local, and tribal government coordination on permitting and review processes (such as conducting reviews concurrently rather than sequentially to the extent practicable); avoiding duplicative reviews; and engaging with stakeholders early in the permitting process;\n(ii) developing mechanisms to better communicate priorities and resolve disputes among agencies at the national and regional levels;\n(iii) institutionalizing use of the Dashboard, working with the CIO to enhance the Dashboard, and utilizing other cost-effective information technology systems to share environmental and project-related information with the public, project sponsors, and permit reviewers; and\n(iv) identifying timeframes and Member Agency responsibilities for the implementation of each proposed action."},{"char_end":195683,"char_start":194719,"text":"Executive Order 13563 of January 18, 2011 (Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review), states that our regulatory system “must measure, and seek to improve, the actual results of regulatory requirements.” To promote this goal, that Executive Order requires agencies not merely to conduct a single exercise, but to engage in “periodic review of existing significant regulations.” Pursuant to section 6(b) of that Executive Order, agencies are required to develop retrospective review plans to review existing significant regulations in order to “determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed.” The purpose of this requirement is to “make the agency’s regulatory program more effective or less burdensome in achieving the regulatory objectives.”\nIn response to Executive Order 13563, agencies have developed and made available for public comment retrospective review plans that identify over five hundred initiatives."},{"char_end":220346,"char_start":220002,"text":"(iii) Invest in recruiting, training, and retaining talent to further the effective delivery of services to individuals and communities and empower them with best-practice community engagement options, open government transparency methods, equitable policy approaches, technical assistance and capacity building tools, and data-driven practice."},{"char_end":252675,"char_start":251491,"text":"Such recommendations may include sustainably reshoring supply chains and developing domestic supplies, cooperating with allies and partners to identify alternative supply chains, building redundancy into domestic supply chains, ensuring and enlarging stockpiles, developing workforce capabilities, enhancing access to financing, expanding research and development to broaden supply chains, addressing risks due to vulnerabilities in digital products relied on by supply chains, addressing risks posed by climate change, and any other recommendations;\n(x) any executive, legislative, regulatory, and policy changes and any other actions to strengthen the capabilities identified in subsection (c)(iii) of this section, and to prevent, avoid, or prepare for any of the contingencies identified in subsection (c)(iv) of this section; and\n(xi) proposals for improving the Government-wide effort to strengthen supply chains, including proposals for coordinating actions required under this order with ongoing efforts that could be considered duplicative of the work of this order or with existing Government mechanisms that could be used to implement this order in a more effective manner."},{"char_end":253471,"char_start":252925,"text":"As soon as practicable following the submission of the reports required under section 4 of this order, the APNSA and the APEP, in coordination with the heads of appropriate agencies, shall provide to the President one or more reports reviewing the actions taken over the previous year and making recommendations concerning:\n(a) steps to strengthen the resilience of America’s supply chains;\n(b) reforms needed to make supply chain analyses and actions more effective, including statutory, regulatory, procedural, and institutional design changes."},{"char_end":261174,"char_start":261085,"text":"Any provisions of Executive Order 14017 not amended in this order shall remain in effect."},{"char_end":279755,"char_start":278859,"text":"(c) To inform and advise the President, so that he may formulate appropriate and effective civil-rights policies for the Executive Branch, the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy shall convene a monthly meeting attended by the Director of OMB, the Director of OPM, and each deputy agency or department head to:\n(i) hear reports on the prevalence and the economic and social costs of DEI, DEIA, and “environmental justice” in agency or department programs, activities, policies, regulations, guidance, employment practices, enforcement activities, contracts (including set-asides), grants, consent orders, and litigating positions;\n(ii) discuss any barriers to measures to comply with this order; and\n(iii) monitor and track agency and department progress and identify potential areas for additional Presidential or legislative action to advance the policy of equal dignity and respect."},{"char_end":324597,"char_start":324342,"text":"For the purposes of this order:\n(a) “Conditional Sunset Date” means the date a regulation will cease to be effective and be removed from the Code of Federal Regulations, if the agency does not extend the Sunset Date pursuant to section 4(d) of this order."},{"char_end":329395,"char_start":329166,"text":"(a) To the extent consistent with applicable law, each of the Covered Agencies shall issue a sunset rule, effective not later than September 30, 2025, that inserts a Conditional Sunset Date into each of their Covered Regulations."},{"char_end":329654,"char_start":329396,"text":"(b) The sunset rule shall provide that each Covered Regulation in effect on the date of this order shall have a Conditional Sunset Date of 1 year after the effective date of the sunset rule, subject to the process set forth in subsection (d) of this section."},{"char_end":329841,"char_start":329655,"text":"Unless the extension condition specified in subsection (d) of this section is satisfied, agencies will treat Covered Regulations as ceasing to be effective on that date for all purposes."},{"char_end":343858,"char_start":343719,"text":"With your help and cooperation, we hope to move the Government toward a more flexible, effective, and user friendly approach to regulation."},{"char_end":345956,"char_start":345396,"text":"(a) Each agency shall reduce by one-half the frequency of the regularly scheduled reports that the public is required, by rule or by policy, to provide to the Government (from quarterly to semiannually, from semiannually to annually, etc.), unless the department or agency head determines that such action is not legally permissible; would not adequately protect health, safety, or the environment; would be inconsistent with achieving regulatory flexibility or reducing regulatory burdens; or would impede the effective administration of the agency’s program."},{"char_end":362281,"char_start":361614,"text":"Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993, as amended, states, “Each agency shall tailor its regulations to impose the least burden on society, including individuals, businesses of differing sizes, and other entities (including small communities and governmental entities), consistent with obtaining the regulatory objectives, taking into account, among other things, and to the extent practicable, the costs of cumulative regulations.”\nIn the current economic environment, it is especially important for agencies to design regulations in a cost-effective manner consistent with the goals of promoting economic growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation."},{"char_end":371931,"char_start":370122,"text":"The plan shall identify proposed actions and associated timelines to:\n(1) institutionalize or expand best practices or process improvements that agencies are already implementing to improve the efficiency of reviews, while improving outcomes for communities and the environment;\n(2) revise key review and permitting regulations, policies, and procedures (both agency-specific and Government-wide);\n(3) identify high-performance attributes of infrastructure projects that demonstrate how the projects seek to advance existing statutory and policy objectives and how they lead to improved outcomes for communities and the environment, thereby facilitating a faster and more efficient review and permitting process;\n(4) create process efficiencies, including additional use of concurrent and integrated reviews;\n(5) identify opportunities to use existing share-in-cost authorities and other non-appropriated funding sources to support early coordination and project review;\n(6) effectively engage the public and interested stakeholders;\n(7) expand coordination with State, local, and tribal governments;\n(8) strategically expand the use of information technology (IT) tools and identify priority areas for IT investment to replace paperwork processes, enhance effective project siting decisions, enhance interagency collaboration, and improve the monitoring of project impacts and mitigation commitments; and\n(9) identify improvements to mitigation policies to provide project developers with added predictability, facilitate landscape-scale mitigation based on conservation plans and regional environmental assessments, facilitate interagency mitigation plans where appropriate, ensure accountability and the long-term effectiveness of mitigation activities, and utilize innovative mechanisms where appropriate."},{"char_end":388218,"char_start":387794,"text":"(3) Consistent with applicable law and subject to the exceptions described in paragraph 1, consider postponing for 60 days from the date of this memorandum [Jan. 20, 2025] the effective date for any rules that have been published in the Federal Register, or any rules that have been issued in any manner but have not taken effect, for the purpose of reviewing any questions of fact, law, and policy that the rules may raise."},{"char_end":389736,"char_start":389365,"text":"It also includes any “regulatory action,” as defined in section 3(e) of Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993 [set out above], as amended, and any “guidance document” as defined in section 2(b) of Executive Order 13891 of October 9, 2019 (Promoting the Rule of Law Through Improved Agency Guidance Documents) [formerly set out above], when that order was in effect."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10122>EO:12630","names_target":false,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Relative date candidate uses only an expressly named base and term; confirm applicability. Indirect parent membership is an unconfirmed lead.","provision_label":"Sec. 4.","reaches_target_via":"EO:11246 as amended","savings_phrases":["Significantly larger savings are anticipated as the plans are implemented and as action is taken on additional initiatives.","In implementing and improving their retrospective review plans, and in considering retrospective review suggestions from the public, agencies shall give priority, consistent with law, to those initiatives that will produce significant quantifiable monetary savings or significant quantifiable reductions in paperwork burdens while protecting public health, welfare, safety, and our environment.","For example, automatic enrollment and automatic escalation in retirement savings plans have made it easier to save for the future, and have helped Americans accumulate billions of dollars in additional retirement savings.","(b) In implementing the policy directives in section (a), agencies shall:\n(i) identify opportunities to help qualifying individuals, families, communities, and businesses access public programs and benefits by, as appropriate, streamlining processes that may otherwise limit or delay participation—for example, removing administrative hurdles, shortening wait times, and simplifying forms;\n(ii) improve how information is presented to consumers, borrowers, program beneficiaries, and other individuals, whether as directly conveyed by the agency, or in setting standards for the presentation of information, by considering how the content, format, timing, and medium by which information is conveyed affects comprehension and action by individuals, as appropriate;\n(iii) identify programs that offer choices and carefully consider how the presentation and structure of those choices, including the order, number, and arrangement of options, can most effectively promote public welfare, as appropriate, giving particular consideration to the selection and setting of default options; and\n(iv) review elements of their policies and programs that are designed to encourage or make it easier for Americans to take specific actions, such as saving for retirement or completing education programs.","Such guidance shall address, among other things, processes for standardizing the measurement and estimation of regulatory costs; standards for determining what qualifies as new and offsetting regulations; standards for determining the costs of existing regulations that are considered for elimination; processes for accounting for costs in different fiscal years; methods to oversee the issuance of rules with costs offset by savings at different times or different agencies; and emergencies and other circumstances that might justify individual waivers of the requirements of this section.","Beginning with the Regulatory Plans, as required under Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993 (Regulatory Planning and Review) [set out above], as amended, or any successor order for fiscal year 2026, and for each fiscal year thereafter:\n(a) The head of each agency shall identify on an aggregated basis, for regulations that increase incremental cost, the offsetting regulations described in section 3(c) of this order, and provide the agency’s best approximation of the total costs or savings associated with each new regulation or repealed regulation.","Through the implementation of Executive Order 13604 of March 22, 2012 (Improving Performance of Federal Permitting and Review of Infrastructure Projects), executive departments and agencies (agencies) have achieved better outcomes for communities and the environment and realized substantial time savings in review and permitting by prioritizing the deployment of resources to specific sectors and projects, and by implementing best-management practices."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1988-03-15","target_id":"EO:10122","verb":"amend"}

  Text: [T72f9bf1ce2b0cb61f2a65ca7](#t72f9bf1ce2b0cb61f2a65ca7); absolute characters 47332–47965
- **ACT:EO:10122>EO:13279**; S811daae42fc568099f6090d6; {"actor_id":"EO:13279","char_end":11096,"char_start":10265,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":5656,"char_start":4492,"text":"In formulating and implementing policies that have implications for faith-\nbased and community organizations, agencies that administer social service \nprograms supported with Federal financial assistance shall, to the extent \npermitted by law, be guided by the following fundamental principles: \n(a) Federal financial assistance for social service programs should be dis-\ntributed in the most effective and efficient manner possible; \n(b) The Nation ’s social service capacity will benefit if all eligible organiza-\ntions, including faith-based and other community organizations, are able \nto compete on an equal footing for Federal financial assistance used to \nsupport social service programs; \n(c) No organization should be discriminated against on the basis of religion \nor religious belief in the administration or distribution of Federal financial \nassistance under social service programs; \n(d) All organizations that receive Federal financial assistance under social \nservices programs should be prohibited from discriminating against bene-\nficiaries or potential beneficiaries of the social services programs on the \nbasis of religion or religious belief."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:10122>EO:13279","names_target":false,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date. Indirect parent membership is an unconfirmed lead.","provision_label":"Sec. 4.","reaches_target_via":"EO:11246 as amended","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2002-12-12","target_id":"EO:10122","verb":"amend"}

io n s G overning  P a y m e n t o f D is a b il­\ni t y R etir e m e n t P a y, H o sp it a l iz a t io n, \nand  R e - e x am in a tio n o f M em bers and  \nF orm er M em bers of  th e U n ifo r m ed \nS ervices ”\nBy virtue of and pursuant to the au­\nthority vested in me by section 414 (b)  \nof the Career Compensation Act of 1949,  \napproved October 12, 1949 (Public Law  \n351, 81st Congress), and as President of  \nthe United States and Commander in  \nChief of the Armed Forces of the United  \nStates, I hereby amend Executive Order  \nNo. 10122 of April 14, 1950, entitled  \n“Regulations Governing Payment of Dis­\nability Retirement Pay, Hospitalization,  \nand Re-examination of Members and  \nFormer Members of the Uniformed  \nServices”, as follows, such amendments  \nto be effective October 15, 1952:\nSection 3 of such order is amended to  \nread as follows; “All duties, powers, and  \nfunctions incident to the hospitalization,  \nexcept as provided in section 5 of this  \norder, and re-examination of members  \nof the uniformed services placed on the  \ntemporary disability retired list under  \nthe provisions of the Career Compensa­\ntion Act of 1949 shall be vested in the  \nSecretary concerned.”\nSection 5 of such order is amended to  \nread as follows: “All duties, powers, and  \nfunctions incident to the hospitalization  \nof members or former members of the  \nuniformed services placed on the tempo­\nrary disability retired list or permanently  \nretired for physical disability or receiving  \ndisability retirement pay who require  \nhospitalization for chronic diseases shall  \nbe vested in the Administrator of Vet-\nerans’  Affairs: Provided,  that all duties,  \npowers, and functions incident to the  \nhospitalization of such members or  \nformer members who are or have been ad­\nmitted to hospitals under the jurisdiction  \nof the uniformed services before October  \n15, 1952, may be exercised by the Secre­\ntary concerned until April 15,1953: Pro­\nvided further,  that all the duties, powers,  \nand functions incident to hospitalization  \nfor such members or former members  \nwho have completed twenty or more  \nyears of active duty, as defined in section  \n412 of the Career Compensation Act of  \n1949, who require hospitalization for  \nchronic diseases other than blindness,  \nneuropsychiatrie or psychiatric disorders  \nand tuberculosis, who are acceptable  \nmedically to the Commanding Officer of a  \nservice hospital, and who elect not to  \nreceive hospitalization in Veterans Ad­\nministration facilities shall be vested in  \nthe Secretary concerned: And provided  \nfurther,  that for the purpose of this  \norder, the term ‘ chronic diseases’  shall be \nconstrued to include chronic arthritis,  \nmalignancy, psychiatric or neuropsychi­\natrie disorder, neurological disabilities,  \npoliomyelitis with disability residuals  \nand degenerative diseases of the nervous  \nsystem, severe injuries to the nervous  \nsystem including quadriplegics, hémi­\nplégies, and paraplegics, tuberculosis,  \nblindness and deafness requiring defini­\ntive rehabilitation, major amputees, and  \nsuch other diseases as may be so defined  \njointly by the Secretary of Defense, the  \nAdministrator of Veterans’  Affairs, and  \nthe Federal Security Administrator and  \nso described in appropriate regulations  \nof the respective departments and agen­\ncies concerned.","sections_touched":["section 414","Section 3","section 5","Section 5","section ## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.
Preparation attestations never approve legal conclusions or replace whole-case review.

verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["is hereby authorized"],"text":"(a) The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of \nthe Treasury and other officials of the United States Government as appro-\npriate, is hereby authorized to impose on a foreign person any of the sanctions \ndescribed in subsections (b) and (c) of this section, upon determining that \nthe person, on or after the date of this order: \n(i) is responsible for or complicit in, has directly or indirectly engaged \nin, or attempted to engage in, or financed the obstruction, disruption, \nor prevention of efforts to promote a Syria that is stable, unified, and \nat peace with itself and its neighbors, including: \n(A) the convening and conduct of a credible and inclusive Syrian- \nled constitutional process; \n(B) the preparation for and conduct of supervised elections, pursuant \nto the new constitution, that are free and fair and to the highest inter-\nnational standards of transparency and accountability; or \n(C) the development of a Syrian government that is representative and \nreflects the will of the Syrian people; \n(ii) is an adult family member of a person designated under subsection \n(a)(i) of this section; or \n(iii) is responsible for or complicit in, or has directly or indirectly engaged \nin, or attempted to engage in, the expropriation of property, including \nreal property, for personal gain or political purposes in Syria.’’"},{"char_end":11336,"char_start":10842,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":11336,"context_char_start":10842,"line":160,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary \nof the Treasury, shall examine whether the criteria set forth in section \n7431(a) of the Caesar Act have been met, and on the basis of that examination \nmay, pursuant to the Presidential Memorandum of March 31, 2020 (Delega-\ntion of Certain Functions and Authorities Under the National Defense Author-\nization Act for Fiscal Year 2020), suspend in whole or in part the imposition \nof sanctions otherwise required under the Caesar Act."},{"char_end":11675,"char_start":11337,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":11675,"context_char_start":11337,"line":166,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"If the Secretary of \nState determines to suspend in whole or in part the imposition of such \nsanctions, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the \nTreasury, shall provide the briefing to the appropriate congressional commit-\ntees required by section 7431(b) of the Caesar Act within 30 days of such \ndetermination."},{"char_end":12023,"char_start":11676,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":12023,"context_char_start":11676,"line":171,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"Further, the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Sec-\nretary of the Treasury, shall continue to review the situation in Syria, and \nif the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, \ndetermines that the criteria set forth in section 7431(a) are no longer met, \nthe Secretary of State shall reimpose sanctions."},{"char_end":12541,"char_start":12409,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":12541,"context_char_start":12409,"line":181,"pdf_page":3,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Secretary of State shall submit to the appropriate congressional \ncommittees the report required under section 5(b) of that Act."},{"char_end":13992,"char_start":13804,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":13992,"context_char_start":13804,"line":202,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(b) The Secretary of State shall transmit this waiver determination and \nreport as required by sections 307(d)(1)(B) and (d)(2) of the CBW Act to \nthe appropriate congressional committees."},{"char_end":14066,"char_start":13993,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":14066,"context_char_start":13993,"line":204,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"This waiver shall be effective \n20 days after it has been so transmitted."},{"char_end":14645,"char_start":14107,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":14645,"context_char_start":14107,"line":206,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(a) The Secretary of State, in consulta-\ntion with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Attorney General, shall \ntake all appropriate action with respect to the designation of al-Nusrah \nFront, also known as Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham and other aliases, as a Foreign \nTerrorist Organization under 8 U.S.C. 1189 and as a Specially Designated \nGlobal Terrorist under 50 U.S.C. 1702 and Executive Order 13224, as well \nas the designation of Abu Muhammad al-Jawlani, commonly known as \nAhmed al-Sharaa, as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist."},{"char_end":15111,"char_start":14647,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":15111,"context_char_start":14647,"line":214,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(b) The Secretary of State shall take all appropriate action to review \nthe designation of Syria as a State Sponsor of Terrorism consistent with \nsection 1754(c) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year \n2019 (Public Law 115–232; 50 U.S.C. 4813(c)), section 40 of the Arms \nExport Control Act (Public Law 90–629, as amended; 22 U.S.C. 2780), and \nsection 620A of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (Public Law 87–195, \nas amended; 22 U.S.C. 2371)."},{"char_end":15491,"char_start":15137,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":15491,"context_char_start":15137,"line":221,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Secretary of State shall take appropriate steps \nto advance United States policy objectives at the United Nations to support \na Syria that is stable and at peace and to support Syrian efforts to counter \nterrorism and comply with its responsibilities and obligations concerning \nweapons of mass destruction, including chemical and biological weapons."},{"char_end":15899,"char_start":15664,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":15899,"context_char_start":15664,"line":228,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["are hereby authorized"],"text":"The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, \nand the Secretary of Commerce, as appropriate, are hereby authorized to \ntake such actions, including adopting rules and regulations, as may be \nnecessary to implement this order."},{"char_end":16466,"char_start":16094,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":16466,"context_char_start":16094,"line":234,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["is authorized"],"text":"The Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, \nthe Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of Transportation, as appro-\npriate, is authorized to exercise the functions and authorities conferred \nupon the President in section 5 of the Syria Accountability Act and to \nredelegate these functions and authorities consistent with applicable law."},{"char_end":16618,"char_start":16468,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":16618,"context_char_start":16468,"line":239,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"All agencies of the United States shall take all appropriate measures within \ntheir authority to implement this order, consistent with applicable law."},{"char_end":16963,"char_start":16649,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":16963,"context_char_start":16649,"line":241,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; or \n(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget \nrelating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals."},{"char_end":17355,"char_start":16965,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":17355,"context_char_start":16965,"line":247,"pdf_page":4,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory;
